one_liner: Aircall has a broad REST API with webhooks. Customer admins self-generate an API ID and token (Basic auth) from their own account, and OAuth is limited to Tech Partners. No MCP server was found on the supplied pages.
auth_notes: Basic Auth (api_id:api_token) is generated by an Aircall customer in the dashboard. OAuth 2.0 (authorization code) needs client_id and client_secret from Aircall, issued only after Technology Partner approval, so it is not self-serve. A multi-user toolkit would use per-customer Basic keys unless partnered.
access_notes: Keys come from an existing Aircall customer account, and private apps need no review. The homepage offers "TRY FOR FREE", but no fetched page says whether API keys work during a trial or whether a paid plan is required. The Messaging API additionally requires the Professional plan for direct use. Treat paid_plan as the most defensible but unconfirmed value.
blocker_notes: A customer Aircall account is needed to generate keys, and the pages do not confirm a free path. OAuth for multi-tenant use requires Tech Partner approval. Messaging API direct access needs the Professional plan.

evidence.quote: Aircall Public API is a classic REST API.
We can call back any endpoint of your choice, each time an event occurs on an Aircall account
If you are an Aircall customer, building for your own Aircall account only, the Basic Auth flow will do the trick.
Before starting building the OAuth flow for your app, you will need to get OAuth client_id and client_secret from Aircall.
It's the fastest way to get started — no review process, no marketplace listing, and no OAuth flow required.
